analysis:
Documentation-only changes. docs/architecture/README.md: only the 'Last updated' stamp (2026-10-09) is visible in the supplied head text; the link tables are unchanged context. docs/architecture/cache-aware-routing.md: the date stamp is bumped, and a new paragraph under '### Protocol v2 proof' (head hunk ~line 261) says live and checkpoint precision belong to the provider's concrete storage identity. Native-exact, lossy-to-native and live-packed checkpoints use distinct layouts and namespaces. The proof authenticates the token prefix and a compatible checkpoint, not lossless reconstruction or latency. Legacy resident-page and native tensor snapshot formats stay bypassed for live-packed precision. Provider precision choices do not change proof, receipt or billing authority. The paragraph links to kv-cache-quantization.md.

This restates existing boundaries and weakens none of them. It claims no change to coordinator proof, cacheSalt scoping, receipts, TTL, or the at-rest posture covered by T-041 (SEC-035). No code, config, wire or authorization behavior changed in the supplied units. I found no invalidated threat assumptions. One coverage limit: kv-cache-quantization.md, the linked page, and the provider code that implements live-packed precision were not supplied. The claims that they bypass legacy formats and leave receipt and billing authority unchanged are therefore unverified here. A pass covering those files should check that the precision-specific namespaces keep the HMAC lookup-tag and cacheSalt scoping described in T-041.
